# rt/vec

> Growable arrays of 64-bit words (ints, or pointers and strings with as).

truck [rt](../rt.md) · [source](../../../registry/rt/vec.pkg)

```
let v = vec_new()
vec_push(v, 10)
vec_push(v, "name" as int)      // any one-word value, converted with as
print vec_get(v, 0)             // 10
print vec_get(v, 1) as str      // name
```

There are no generic types, so a `Vec` holds words and typed code
converts with `as` when storing and loading. Reading or writing past the
end stops the program with `rt/vec: index out of range`.

| function | does |
|---|---|
| `vec_new() -> ptr Vec` | an empty vector |
| `vec_len(v: ptr Vec) -> int` | number of items |
| `vec_push(v: ptr Vec, x: int)` | append, growing the storage when full |
| `vec_get(v: ptr Vec, i: int) -> int` | item `i` |
| `vec_set(v: ptr Vec, i: int, x: int)` | replace item `i` |
| `vec_pop(v: ptr Vec) -> int` | remove and return the last item |
| `vec_last(v: ptr Vec) -> int` | the last item |
| `vec_clear(v: ptr Vec)` | remove every item (keeps the storage) |

## Library code

Merged into every program that uses this package.

```
struct Vec
  data: [int]
  len: int
end

fn vec_new() -> ptr Vec
  let v = new Vec
  v.data = make([int], 8)
  return v
end

fn vec_len(v: ptr Vec) -> int
  return v.len
end

fn vec_push(v: ptr Vec, x: int)
  if v.len == len(v.data)
    let bigger = make([int], len(v.data) * 2)
    mem_copy((&bigger[0]) as ptr u8, (&v.data[0]) as ptr u8, v.len * 8)
    v.data = bigger
  end
  v.data[v.len] = x
  v.len = v.len + 1
end

fn vec_check(v: ptr Vec, i: int)
  if i < 0 || i >= v.len
    rt_panic("rt/vec: index out of range")
  end
end

fn vec_get(v: ptr Vec, i: int) -> int
  vec_check(v, i)
  return v.data[i]
end

fn vec_set(v: ptr Vec, i: int, x: int)
  vec_check(v, i)
  v.data[i] = x
end

fn vec_pop(v: ptr Vec) -> int
  vec_check(v, v.len - 1)
  v.len = v.len - 1
  return v.data[v.len]
end

fn vec_last(v: ptr Vec) -> int
  vec_check(v, v.len - 1)
  return v.data[v.len - 1]
end

fn vec_clear(v: ptr Vec)
  v.len = 0
end
```
